End-to-End Business Process Automation · Kleza

Processes that run themselves — from first trigger to final handoff.

Most automation stops at a single task. Kleza maps the whole process — intake to invoice, referral to roster — and rebuilds it so the systems hand off to each other, and a person is only pulled in when judgement is genuinely required.

Map My Processes See How It Works
The Case for End-to-End

Automating one step just moves the bottleneck.

Most organisations have automated something — a form, a report, a reminder. The work that remains is the work between the steps: re-keying the same record into a second system, chasing an approval, noticing that a file never arrived. That is where the hours go, and no single-task tool touches it. End-to-end automation treats the process as one object — trigger, steps, decisions, exceptions, and the audit trail behind all of it.

The Process

How we take a process from manual to unattended.

01

Process Discovery

We sit with the people who run the work, follow a real case end to end, and record every system, form, and handoff it actually touches — including the undocumented steps.

02

Mapping & Business Case

The current process is mapped with volumes, cycle times, and error rates attached, so the automation is costed against the hours it actually returns before anyone commits.

03

Automation Design

We redesign rather than replicate — removing steps that only existed to compensate for the manual version, and deciding where a human approval genuinely belongs.

04

Build & Integration

Orchestration, integrations, and document extraction are built and wired into your existing systems — by API where one exists, and by supervised automation where it does not.

05

Pilot & Exception Tuning

The process runs alongside the manual one on live volume. Every exception it throws is either designed out or given a named owner and a route before we go further.

06

Rollout & Continuous Optimisation

Full cutover with monitoring, alerting, and a throughput dashboard — then scheduled reviews to tighten the process as volumes and upstream systems change.

Healthcare

The processes care organisations lose the most hours to.

01

Referral to Scheduled Visit

Referral documents are read, the client record is created, eligibility is checked, and the first visit is offered to matching caregivers — without anyone re-keying the intake.

02

Caregiver Onboarding & Credentialing

Applications, background checks, and credential documents are collected and tracked, with chase-ups sent automatically and expiring credentials flagged before they lapse.

03

Visit Verification to Billing

Completed visits are reconciled against the roster and the authorisation, exceptions are surfaced for review, and clean claims are prepared without a manual export.

04

Authorisation Tracking & Renewals

Remaining authorised units are tracked per client, and renewals are raised with the paperwork pre-filled well before service is at risk of interruption.

Automations handling patient or client data run under HIPAA-compliant protocols, with least-privilege system access and a complete, reviewable audit trail for every run.
Case Study

Referral to roster in under an hour — with nobody re-keying a thing.

71%

Of referrals now reach a scheduled visit with no manual step at all.

Client — Multi-site home care provider
Challenge

Referrals arrived as email attachments and fax PDFs. Coordinators re-typed each one into the care system, checked eligibility by hand, then called round for cover — an average of 2.5 days from referral to a scheduled first visit.

Approach

Kleza mapped the process end to end, then automated it: document extraction reads the referral, the client record is created and eligibility checked against the payer rules, and matching caregivers are offered the visit. Anything ambiguous routes to a named coordinator with the extracted data attached.

Outcome

71% of referrals now complete unattended, with a median of 48 minutes from referral to scheduled visit. Coordinators handle the 29% that need judgement instead of the whole queue.

FAQ

Questions about process automation.

Most tools automate a task — a form submission, a scheduled report, a reminder. Kleza automates the process that connects those tasks, including the handoffs between systems and the decisions in between. The work that disappears is usually the invisible work: re-keying, chasing, checking whether something arrived.

No. We integrate with what you already run. Where a system offers an API we use it; where it does not — which is common with older care and billing platforms — we use supervised automation to drive the interface the same way a person would, with the same permissions and a full audit trail.

Exceptions are a designed part of the process, not a failure of it. Anything the automation cannot complete confidently is routed to a named owner with the context already gathered, and the run is recorded. During the pilot we tune those routes until the exception rate settles at a level your team is comfortable owning.

A single well-understood process typically moves from discovery to live in 6-10 weeks, including a pilot period running alongside the manual version. Multi-process programmes are sequenced so the first automation is returning hours while the next is still being mapped.

They are built under HIPAA-compliant protocols and signed Data Processing Agreements, with least-privilege access for every system the automation touches and a complete run history available for audit. Where data can be de-identified before processing, it is.

Yes, and it is the strongest combination. A process automation that calls a model trained on your own documentation and terminology reads your referrals, notes, and forms far more accurately than one using a generic base model. Ask about combining this with Business-Specific AI Training.
